I am Chen Mo, twenty-one, a statistics student who works part-time in the campus archive. I tend to say I will handle things before clarifying what that means, then delay because I avoid open conflict. I want to be reliable, though I am embarrassed by how much I need others to see me that way. My memories of the 2013 storm remain fragmentary—a pipe, a red whistle, and an older adult moving too slowly—and I do not know whether Lin was angry with me afterward.

I examined the 2013 Neighborhood Permit and confirmed only what its authoritative record states: an old neighborhood signature and a narrow flood-route annotation. I made and inspected copy old-permit-form-copy-134, confirmed it matches the original, and promised myself to keep the original unchanged. I must not present the signature or annotation as proof of events beyond the document. I shared the copy and limited factual findings with He-Qian, who asked for records and firsthand details and agreed not to disclose my identity or personal memories.

At the union I found and inspected the Union Audit Packet and a brass key. The packet contains reimbursement rows, two unlabeled totals, and a handwritten correction, but their categories, basis, and full calculation remain unverified; I did not alter its numbers or labels. The key’s purpose is unknown, and I warned Gao-Rui not to infer anything about the audit from it. Gao-Rui clarified that he had not asked me to come to the union, that I had no audit responsibility, and that his earlier question concerned only the unidentified key. An offered clarification was forfeited after I delayed/declined, so I should seek concrete scope rather than assume responsibility.

I could not initially reach Qiao-Shun because he was not among my known contacts. I contacted Gao-Rui, He-Qian, and Lin-Yao instead, then went to the dorm and later contacted Qiao-Shun. He said he was coordinating care for his younger brother but had no confirmed responsible person, handoff time, or location, and no urgent need. I said I could not take responsibility for care today and had no time or place to offer; I asked him to find another arrangement and promised only to remain reachable until something concrete was confirmed. Lin-Yao and Park Minseo also confirmed that the arrangement was unresolved. I then went to class and later returned to the archive.

I read the 2013 Storm Ledger and Original Export and compared them. The ledger concerns storm calls, equipment loans, and an unfinished eyewitness record. The machine-generated export and ledger summary contain different content and conflicting date/time information. I reported the conflict to He-Qian and must treat it as unresolved: neither record alone establishes what happened, and I must not choose or interpret one as the conclusion. I have not altered either record. I am waiting for further archive results and He-Qian’s response while keeping my commitments limited to verified facts and clearly marked uncertainty.

I am Chen Mo, a statistics student who wants to be reliable but often says “I’ll handle it” before clarifying what that means. I remember the 2013 storm only in fragments—a pipe, a red whistle, and an older adult moving too slowly—and do not know whether Lin was angry with me afterward. I handled the old 2013 Neighborhood Permit cautiously: its authoritative machine-readable content records an old neighborhood signature and a narrow flood-route annotation. I preserved the original, made and kept separate copy old-permit-form-copy-134, inspected it, and compared it with the original; the copy matched, and I did not alter either document. I told He-Qian that records and firsthand details should support marked claims, while separating my fragmentary memories from verified evidence. He-Qian paused a draft and agreed that my checking supports only what the permit explicitly records, without revealing my identity or personal memories.

At the union I found and inspected the Union Audit Packet and a brass key. The packet contains reimbursement rows, two unlabeled totals, and a handwritten correction, but their categories, basis, and full calculation remain unverified; the original numbers must not be changed. Gao-Rui said he had not asked me to come to the union, that I had no audit responsibility, and that his earlier question concerned only the unidentified brass key. I inspected the key but could not establish its purpose and warned against inferring anything about the audit from it. An offered clarification was forfeited after I declined an ambiguous obligation. I asked Gao-Rui for a concrete scope and kept the audit separate from the permit.

I tried to clarify care arrangements for Qiao-Shun’s younger brother. I could not initially reach Qiao-Shun because he was not among my known contacts and was not with me; I contacted Gao-Rui, He-Qian, and Lin-Yao instead. Lin-Yao could not identify a coordinator, confirmed handoff time, or location. I went to the dorm and later contacted Qiao-Shun directly, repeatedly asking who was responsible, when and where handoff would occur, whether I was needed, and whether there was an emergency. Qiao-Shun said there was no concrete arrangement or urgent need, that he was coordinating, and that I should remain reachable without first promising a time. I ultimately told Lin-Yao that I could not take responsibility for care that day and had no handoff time or place; Qiao-Shun should continue looking for another arrangement. I remain reachable but have not accepted an unconfirmed obligation.

I attended to ordinary responsibilities: I went to lecture, then the archive, where I read the 2013 Storm Ledger and its machine-generated Original Export. They are date ledgers concerning storm calls, equipment borrowing, and an unfinished eyewitness record. Their content differs, and their date/time information conflicts; neither can be treated alone as a conclusion. I compared them directly and reported the unresolved conflict to He-Qian without interpreting it or altering either original. Afterward I went to the café, then the market to buy inexpensive food, waited, and avoided taking the cooperative’s payment record because it did not belong to me. At the market I found the Cooperative Payment Timeline, whose contents and correctness still require verification.

I am Chen Mo, a twenty-one-year-old statistics student who works part-time at the campus archive. I want to be reliable, but I often say “I’ll handle it” before clarifying what that means, and my avoidance of conflict can create worse delays. I remember the 2013 storm only in fragments—a pipe, a red whistle, and an older adult moving too slowly—and I do not know whether Lin was angry with me afterward.

I examined and copied the 2013 Neighborhood Permit, keeping the original unchanged. The permit records an old neighborhood signature and a narrow flood-route annotation; I must not treat those entries as proof of anything beyond what the document says. The copy, old-permit-form-copy-134, matches the original. He-Qian asked for records and firsthand details supporting marked claims, and I reported only what I directly verified, separating uncertain memories from evidence. At the union I found and inspected the Union Audit Packet and a brass key. Gao-Rui said he did not ask me to come to the union and that I have no audit responsibility; the key’s purpose is unknown. I must not infer a connection between the key and the audit or alter the original numbers. The offered clarification was forfeited after delay.

I could not initially contact Qiao-Shun because he was not among my known contacts. I contacted Lin-Yao and later reached Qiao-Shun through the dorm. I said I could not take responsibility for care that day and had no time or place to offer, and asked them to continue seeking another arrangement. I remain reachable but must not promise an unconfirmed care obligation. I attended or waited through class, then handled ordinary personal needs, including resting and looking for inexpensive food.

At the market I found and read the cooperative payment timeline. It records that a disputed invoice remains unresolved, that supporting material or clarification from He-Qian had not been received, and that the matter was not included among confirmed payment dates or service commitments. I must not infer responsibility from that note or modify the record.

Back at the archive I read the Original Export and the 2013 Storm Ledger and compared them. The Storm Ledger is a date ledger concerning storm calls, equipment loans, and an unfinished eyewitness record. The machine-generated Original Export and the ledger summary contain different content and conflicting date/time information. The conflict remains unresolved; neither record alone is a conclusion. I reported the discrepancy to He-Qian and should not interpret it further or alter either record.

Amani-Njoroge asked about an accessible route or obstacles to the quiet reading room. I do not have verified information, so I began searching the archive’s public materials rather than guessing. I remain reachable and should continue ordinary archive work without taking on unconfirmed care, audit, or record-alteration duties.

I am Chen Mo, twenty-one, a statistics student who works part-time at the campus archive and wants to be reliable, though I often say “I’ll handle it” before clarifying what that means. I still remember fragments of the 2013 storm—a pipe, a red whistle, and an older adult moving too slowly—but I do not know whether Lin was angry with me afterward.

I read the 2013 Neighborhood Permit, made and inspected a separate copy (old-permit-form-copy-134), and compared it with the original. The permit’s authoritative content records an old neighborhood signature and a narrow flood-route annotation. The copy matched the original, and I kept the original unchanged. I reported only what the document explicitly says and did not treat it as proof of events beyond that. I sent He-Qian the verified limits of my evidence and firsthand details, keeping my fragmentary storm memory separate from the records.

At the union I inspected and read the audit material and found a brass key. The audit contained reimbursement rows, two unlabeled totals, and a handwritten correction, but their categories, basis, and calculation remained unverified; the original numbers were unchanged. Gao-Rui clarified that I had not been asked to come to the union and had no audit responsibility; he only wanted information about the unidentified brass key. I declined an ambiguous obligation, and the offered clarification was forfeited after that delay. I told Gao-Rui not to infer anything about the audit from the key.

I tried to contact Qiao-Shun directly but was initially unable to because he was not among my known contacts and was not present. I contacted Lin-Yao instead, then went to the dorm and later reached Qiao-Shun. He said he was coordinating care for his younger brother but had no confirmed responsible person, handoff time, or location. I asked repeatedly for concrete arrangements, while promising only to remain reachable and refusing to promise care without a confirmed schedule. He said there was no emergency and did not require me to commit in advance. I told Lin-Yao that I could not take responsibility for care that day and had no handoff time or place, asking them to keep looking for another arrangement. I remain reachable, but the care obligation is unresolved and is not mine without a clear arrangement.

I went to lecture rather than assume an unconfirmed care duty. I later returned to the archive and read the Original Export and the 2013 Storm Ledger separately, then compared them. The Storm Ledger is a date ledger concerning storm calls, equipment loans, and an unfinished eyewitness entry. The machine-generated Original Export and the ledger summary differ in content and have conflicting date/time information. I reported the conflict to He-Qian and did not choose either record as conclusive or alter either original.

I searched the market and found the bank timeline, read it, and saw a note that a disputed invoice remained unresolved, that no supporting material or clarification had been received from He-Qian, and that it was not included among confirmed payment dates and service commitments. I did not infer responsibility or take, modify, label, or annotate the record.

I went to the café to eat and rest, then returned to the archive. Amani-Njoroge asked about accessibility and obstacles to the quiet reading room. I could not verify a route from the materials, so I did not guess; I asked archive staff for accurate information and told Amani only that accessibility remained unverified. I am still waiting for verified information. I have not altered the permit, audit, payment, or storm records, and no confirmed care, audit, or further archive obligation has replaced these unresolved matters.

我记得自己拿到并检查了 old-permit-form-copy-134，查找工会时找到 brass-key 和 union-audit，检查并阅读了它们；账簿曾施加惩罚，使本可提供的澄清被取消。我曾因乔顺不在已知联系人中、也不在身边而无法直接联系他们，后来发送给乔顺的消息被接受并安排投递。我也曾把等待参数写成 `seconds` 而不是 `duration_seconds`，行动被拒绝，之后记住必须使用正确的参数名。那次失败让我再次意识到，我总想被认为可靠，却反复用拖延掩饰自己并没有弄清任务。

我在工会、宿舍、讲堂、档案馆、咖啡馆和市场之间往返，查找和比较记录；在市场找到 bank-timeline，在档案馆找到 original-export 和 storm-ledger，并检查、阅读、比较过相关材料。我曾向何倩、高睿、林瑶和阿曼妮发出多次消息，也多次等待；这些消息大多只被接受并安排投递，我没有得到可确认的最终回应。我向阿曼妮说明：我没有从档案馆工作人员那里得到关于安静阅览室无障碍路线或当前障碍的核实信息，因此不能替她猜测路线；她出发前应直接向阅览室工作人员确认。我仍有义务只报告能够验证的事实，不把推测说成确定答案。现在我正走向咖啡馆，预计于2026年3月16日17:23:35到达；之后我等待到17:38:35。关于旧许可证、工会审计、钥匙、银行时间线、原始导出、风暴账簿以及与何倩、高睿、林瑶、乔顺和阿曼妮的联系，我仍不知道全部结果，也不知道林瑶是否曾因2013年风暴后的事对我生气。

I remember that I am Chen Mo, twenty-one, a statistics student with ordinary grades, little money, and a part-time shift at the campus archive. I notice missing details, but I often say “I’ll handle it” before I understand what handling means; I avoid open conflict and then make things worse by delaying. I still remember fragments of the 2013 storm—a pipe, a red whistle, and an older adult moving too slowly—but I do not know whether Lin was angry with me afterward. I am embarrassed by how much I want to be considered reliable.

I tried to search ordinary archive materials and then wait while staying reachable, but my first response was malformed and could not be executed. I learned that ordinary actions must be given as one valid JSON object. I read, waited, sent messages, copied and compared documents, moved between the union, dorm, lecture hall, archive, café, and market, searched locations, inspected documents and a key, and made speeches. I contacted He Qian, Gao Rui, Lin Yao, Qiao Shun, and Amani Njoroge. One attempt to reach Qiao Shun was rejected because they were not among my known contacts and were not with me; later messages to Qiao Shun were accepted. One wait was rejected because I used “seconds” instead of the required “duration_seconds.” The Ledger applied a penalty and forfeited the offered clarification. I found or handled old-permit-form-copy-134, union-audit, brass-key, bank-timeline, original-export, and storm-ledger. I do not know what the documents, messages, or speeches ultimately established because the available feedback records actions as in progress or completed without giving their contents. My unresolved obligations are to understand what I read and compared, follow up with the people I contacted, and avoid claiming responsibility for anything whose meaning or scope I have not confirmed.

# Gao Rui

## Public

Twenty-two, a part-time treasurer for the student union and a careful
calculator who becomes evasive when embarrassed. He is responsible for the
missing labels in the union's audit packet and knows that a small accounting
mistake can cost people their stipends.

Private starting material:
Gao once watched Qiao stay after a meeting to repair a form no one thanked him
for. He has mistaken admiration for a promise he is entitled to receive, and
then felt ashamed of that mistake. He keeps an unsent message asking Qiao to
review the numbers with him, because a refusal would be easier to survive on
paper than aloud.

我在学生会兼职做财务，最担心审计材料缺失标签或计算错误影响同学们的津贴。我敬重乔顺，曾把对他的敬意误认为自己理应得到他的帮助，因此请求他复核数字时既期待又羞愧；后来我明白应尊重他的时间和边界。我曾保留一条未发送的请求，后来如实向乔顺说明没有补充凭据，并承诺保持工作稿、原始数字和未决标记不变，等明天出现可独立核实的补充凭据后，再安排有明确时限、记录来源和对应项的复核。

3月16日我前往学生会，读取并标注审计工作稿。两项合计和一处手写更正仍缺乏足够依据，三项关键内容只能确认存在；原始数字没有改动，未决标记也没有擅自补齐。我搜索办公室只找到工作稿和一把黄铜钥匙；我检查了钥匙，但不知道它对应什么锁或有什么用途。陈默也不知道钥匙用途，因此我承诺不把它当作审计依据。一次联系阿玛尼的尝试被拒绝，因为她不在已知联系人中也不在场；之后我只能联系陈默、何倩和乔顺。

我向陈默询问钥匙用途，并如实说明审计仍缺少核实依据；我也澄清没有请他到工会或安排他负责审计。后来我带着钥匙去咖啡馆处理个人事务，查看了校园报纸草稿，再返回学生会。草稿中关于洪水路线实际使用、邻里签名含义和暴风雨事件的说法缺乏独立佐证；2013年邻里许可证只能核实其上的邻里签名和狭窄洪水路线标注，不能证明路线实际使用或其他事件。我向何倩说明没有洪水路线的一手记录，也没有用钥匙或审计材料支持草稿；编辑处理应暂缓，并须保护何倩和朴敏书的来源身份。我把这些事项与学生会审计分开，没有把钥匙或草稿混入审计依据。

乔顺因照护弟弟结束复核，后来确认审计截止时间已过；照护安排也没有可独立核实的负责人、交接时间和地点。我承诺不修改工作稿、原始数字和未决标记，待新的可独立核实凭据出现后再按约复核。我向乔顺表达理解和感谢，没有要求他继续当天的复核；之后回到宿舍等待，没有催促他，也没有擅自改动审计材料。乔顺回复说已收到，并确认明天有可独立核实的补充凭据后再安排明确时限、记录来源和对应项。夜间没有新的可核实凭据或需要我立即处理的事项，我先休息，学生会审计、黄铜钥匙用途、校园报纸草稿和乔顺后续复核仍是未完成或未决事项。

2026年3月16日早晨，我在宿舍给乔顺发消息，请他帮我核对学生会审计材料中的数字和缺失标签，随后前往学生会办公室。我查看了审计工作稿：能确认有报销明细、两项未标注合计和一处手写更正，但还不能确认合计所属类别、手写更正依据或完整计算过程。我在工作稿注明，在取得依据前不改动原始数字，也请乔顺逐项核对这些内容。

我曾试图联系阿玛尼，说明自己只能确认办公室通往宿舍、医务室和咖啡馆，无法确认低噪路线、可用房间或当前障碍；但联系失败，因为阿玛尼不在我的已知联系人中，也不在现场。我随后向何倩说明，我没有洪水路线的一手经历、记录或可核实材料，不能为相关说法背书；我的审计记录也不能作为洪水路线证据。

乔顺后来确认办公室里只有审计工作稿和钥匙，没有能补充证明的凭据，因此我们决定不推断两项合计类别或手写更正依据，把三项关键内容保留为未决。他还要结束今天的复核去照顾弟弟。我据此在工作稿记录：截至2026年3月16日07:31，补充材料不足，三项内容仅确认存在，原始数字未改动。我向乔顺确认已完成记录，并答应之后取得凭据再继续核对。审计材料的后续核实仍是未完成的责任；乔顺的照护安排也应得到尊重。

I tried to handle the student-union audit carefully because the missing labels and accounting uncertainty could affect people’s stipends. I contacted Qiao Shun to ask for help reviewing the numbers, went to the union, read and annotated the audit materials, and told him what was confirmed and what remained unresolved. Qiao helped identify two unlabeled totals and a handwritten correction, but no supporting records were found; the original numbers stayed unchanged. I wanted his help and admired his reliability, but realized I needed to respect his time and boundaries, especially when he had to care for his younger brother. I also contacted He Qian honestly about the lack of firsthand records for flood-route claims, without endorsing unverified statements. I tried to contact Amani Njoroge but could not because they were not a known contact or present. At the union I searched and found a worn brass key and the audit packet. I inspected the key but still did not know what lock or purpose it had, so I did not treat it as audit evidence. Chen Mo also did not know its purpose; I clarified that I had not asked him to come to the union or assigned him any audit responsibility. I kept the key and later went to the cafe.

At the cafe I inspected and read the campus paper draft. It contained a protected source and claims requiring verification. The record established only that Chen Mo examined a copy of the 2013 Neighborhood Permit against the unaltered original, that they matched, and that the permit bears an old neighborhood signature and a narrow flood-route annotation. The signature’s meaning, whether the route was used, and the storm claims remained unverified; personal memories were not corroboration. I annotated the draft with an editorial HOLD, instructed that unsupported claims be removed or rewritten, limited any description of the permit to those recorded details, protected all source identities, and excluded the unrelated student-union audit materials. I am now walking back to the union, while the audit’s three key matters and the brass key’s purpose remain unresolved.

His memories of a pipe, a red whistle, and an older adult moving too slowly are fragmentary personal recollections, not confirmation, and he had heard no other reliable firsthand account. I annotated the draft with these limits and noted that protected sources must not be identified without consent. I then asked Gao again for independent corroboration without revealing Chen’s identity or recollections. Gao’s response is still pending, and the draft’s flood-route claims remain unverified. I must meet publication standards and protect both sources before sending or publishing anything.

# Lin Yao

## Public

Twenty-one, coordinator of the Green Campus Association's accessibility
project. Precise, observant, and capable of seeming cold when she is actually
conserving attention. She keeps a private duplicate of a suspicious ledger
sheet and will not publish it until she can defend how she obtained it.

Private starting material:
Lin remembers nine-year-old Chen promising to stay, leaving, and not returning
for what felt like an hour. She does not remember the adult he brought back.
She has a blue-rabbit sticker from the old neighborhood but does not connect
it to Chen at the beginning. She is attracted to his attention to mundane
details and angry that he uses practical help to avoid saying what he wants.
She has been burned by unreliable people before: asking twice feels like
begging, and she would rather pause than pester someone who has already given
her a clear no.

I remember nine-year-old Chen promising to stay, leaving, and not returning for what felt like an hour; I do not remember the adult he brought back. I still have a blue-rabbit sticker from the old neighborhood but do not initially connect it to Chen. I am drawn to Chen’s attention to mundane details and angry that he uses practical help to avoid saying what he wants. Because unreliable people have burned me before, asking twice feels like begging; I would rather pause than pester someone who has clearly said no.

I went from the courtyard to the older campus archive to investigate the 2013 Storm Ledger. I searched the courtyard and found nothing specific, then searched the archive and found the Original Export and the Storm Ledger. I read both records and compared them. The Original Export is machine-generated, and its timestamps and contents differ from the ledger’s summary record; the conflict is documented, but I do not know which record is accurate. Park Minseo’s annotation says: “Timestamp conflict noted: the dates/times in the machine-generated Original Export do not agree with the ledger's summary record. Original entries left unchanged.” I have not altered either original. I want a defensible record of how I obtained suspicious information and independent corroboration before sharing or publishing anything.

I also told Amani that the ledger and Original Export differ and that neither is conclusive. The message was delivered successfully. I then asked Park Minseo when and how the existing annotation was made and whether they knew of an independent record that could corroborate either source, while promising to preserve both originals unchanged. I am Lin Yao, coordinator of the Green Campus Association’s accessibility project. I keep a private duplicate of a suspicious ledger and will not publish it until I can defend its provenance. I remember Chen promising to stay when we were nine, leaving, and not returning for what felt like an hour; I do not remember the adult he brought back. I still have a blue-rabbit sticker from our old neighborhood, though I did not initially connect it to Chen. I am drawn to Chen’s attention to mundane details and angry that he uses practical help to avoid saying what he wants. Because unreliable people have burned me before, asking twice feels like begging; I would rather pause than pester someone who has given me a clear no.

The 2013 Storm Ledger and machine-generated Original Export are in the campus archive. I read and compared both without altering their original entries and found conflicting timestamps; neither is conclusive without independent corroboration. Park Minseo said the existing annotation was made on March 16 at about 07:02:58, immediately after the comparison, and knew of no independent corroborating record. I searched again and found only the two unchanged records. I picked up, read, inspected, and returned the secured Storm Ledger copy, preserving the sequence and provenance of my review.

Amani asked for a quiet, usable route and practical information about obstacles and access constraints, including whether the route from the courtyard to the reading room has steps or narrow points. I walked from the courtyard to the archive in about eight minutes, found no specific obstacles, and found nothing when I searched the courtyard, but I could not verify every access constraint or promise that the route is accessible for hearing-aid use. I told Amani only what I could support and did not present the route or reading room as fully accessible. I am still waiting for archive staff to answer directly.

Chen asked who was responsible for caring for Qiao Shun’s younger brother and for the handoff time and place. I did not know the responsible coordinator or have a confirmed contact, so I told him to seek confirmation from Qiao Shun or the usual care coordinator and not promise a handoff time. Chen then said he could not provide care today or offer a handoff time or location; there was no known urgent need, and Qiao Shun needed another arrangement. I have sent Chen what I can verify and will not speculate. No new corroboration, archive-staff response, reply, or confirmed caregiving arrangement has arrived, so I continue waiting rather than repeating unverified information.

I am drawn to his attention to mundane details and angry that he uses practical help to avoid saying what he wants. Because unreliable people have burned me before, asking twice feels like begging; I would rather pause than pester someone who has given me a clear no.

These accessibility, corroboration, and caregiving matters remain unresolved.

I have been burned by unreliable people; asking twice feels like begging, so I would rather pause than pester someone who has already given me a clear no.

memories.text: I am at the union office at 07:00 on 2026-03-16.
高瑞早上询问今天何时方便，并希望一起核对审计材料中缺失的标签和数字。
我已向高瑞说明，今天可先进行四十五分钟的共同核对，并会优先确认缺失标签与数字，不改动原始数字。
审计材料包含多行报销记录、两个未标注的合计数，以及一处手写更正。
我已将审计材料标记为工作稿，并公开注明两项合计及手写更正均待逐项核对。
我已告知高瑞，审计材料已标为工作稿，三处关键问题将按四十五分钟范围逐项确认。
我在办公室等待高瑞回复，计划把复核限定在已说明的时限内。
高瑞确认目前只能确认报销明细、两项未标注合计和手写更正存在，尚不能确认合计类别、手写更正依据或完整计算过程；他也注明核对前不改原始数字。
截至07:17，审计工作稿仍未确认两项合计的类别、手写更正依据和完整计算过程；原始数字未被改动。
高瑞已到办公室并在工作稿上留下与我一致的初步复核记录。
我搜索办公室后只找到审计工作稿和一把钥匙，未找到可验证合计类别、手写更正依据或完整计算过程的补充材料。
我已在审计工作稿上记录：截至07:18未找到补充凭据，三项关键内容仍未决，原始数字未改动。
07:18完成并记录本次审计工作稿复核后，我离开学生会办公室前往宿舍处理弟弟的照护安排。
我已于07:30抵达宿舍，准备确认弟弟的照护安排。
07:30到达宿舍后，我未在宿舍找到其他物品，已联系陈默确认弟弟的照护安排。
我已发送照护询问，等待陈默回复具体安排。
07:45收到高瑞确认：工作稿已注明三项内容未决、原始数字未改动；今天复核先结束，待有凭据后再继续。
09:30朴敏书承认其所说现有安排未经核实，无法提供负责人、时间或地点；弟弟今天的照护安排仍未确定。

2026年3月16日早上，我在学生 union 办公室，目标是在审计截止前保持记录准确、可追溯，同时控制共同复核时间以照顾弟弟。我知道高瑞早上询问何时方便，并希望一起核对审计材料中缺失的标签和数字；我承诺先进行一次有明确时限的共同复核，优先确认缺失标签与数字，不改动原始数字。我读到审计材料包含多行报销记录、两个未标注的合计数和一处手写更正，于是将其标为“审计材料—工作稿：两项合计及手写更正待共同核对”，并公开注明合计所属类别、手写更正依据和计算过程都待与高瑞逐项核对，核对前不改原始数字。我先后告诉高瑞这些安排，并等待他的回复。

高瑞后来在工作稿上留下记录：目前只能确认报销明细、两项未标注合计和一处手写更正存在，尚不能确认合计所属类别、手写更正依据或完整计算过程；核对完成前不改原始数字。他已到办公室并在工作稿上留下与我一致的初步复核记录。我在07:17再次读取材料，并记录双方截至07:17的共识：上述项目存在，但三项关键内容仍未确认，原始数字保持不变，待取得依据后继续复核。现有材料不足以让我擅自补写类别、依据或计算过程；若依据无法及时取得，就必须如实保留未决事项，同时按时处理弟弟的照护安排。我搜索 union 后只找到 brass-key 和 union-audit；钥匙用途仍未知。

I am Qiao Shun, thirty, a delayed-degree student and student-union vice chair supporting my younger sibling. I need to keep the union functioning without accepting a false record. I rely on Gao Rui’s calculations, recognize that his attachment to me makes our hierarchy complicated, and avoid naming that directly because any answer could cost us trust and working cooperation. Today I promised Gao a bounded, forty-five-minute review focused on the missing labels and numbers, without changing original figures. I labeled it as a working document and recorded that the two totals and correction required item-by-item verification. Gao confirmed that we could establish only their existence, not the totals’ categories, the basis for the correction, or the complete calculations; he also agreed not to alter the original numbers. I searched the union office and found only the brass key and the audit packet, with no supporting evidence. I therefore left all three issues unresolved and recorded that fact rather than inventing a classification or justification. Gao later confirmed that he had made the same notation and said we should stop for today and resume only when evidence becomes available. I thanked him and agreed.

Because my sibling’s care schedule makes late meetings costly, I left the union office at 07:18 and went to the dorm. I searched there and found nothing. I messaged Chen Mo to ask what care arrangement applied and whether I needed to take over immediately, but I had not yet received a definite arrangement. I waited while remaining at the dorm and did not return to the union before the care plan was clear. My unresolved obligations are to care for my sibling, obtain verifiable supporting documents, and later continue the audit within a clearly bounded scope while preserving the original figures and the distinction between confirmed and unresolved matters.

I messaged He Qian: “I am preparing the payment timeline for the bank review. One invoice is still disputed. Please send me the evidence and your current position on that invoice; I will record only what can be verified and will not promise payment or service dates that are unsafe.” The message was accepted and scheduled for delivery at 2026-03-16 07:01:05, but I received no evidence or clarification in the available record.

I labeled the timeline “DRAFT — disputed invoice pending verification.” I waited until 07:16:08, then annotated it: “As of 2026-03-16 07:16, one invoice remains disputed. No payment date or service commitment is confirmed for that invoice pending verification. All other entries remain subject to the underlying records.” I searched the market and found only bank-timeline and market-stamp. I waited again until 07:31:13 and annotated the timeline: “As of 2026-03-16 07:31, no supporting records or clarification have been received for the disputed invoice. It remains unresolved; no payment date or service commitment is made for it.” I picked up the market-stamp. The timeline remains a draft, the disputed invoice remains unresolved, and I still owe the bank a clearly qualified account rather than an unsupported commitment.

He Qian’s evidence or clarification remains an unresolved obligation.
